slides.title: Tipping Points in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems: Stance on Climate Change Action
slides.tldr: LLM-POWERED AGENT-BASED MODELING OF SOCIAL TIPPING POINTS
slides.highlight: This research uses LLM-powered agent-based models to study social tipping points and opinion dynamics regarding climate change, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation using LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: LLM-powered agent simulations show abrupt climate stance shifts, but results are heavily skewed by model biases.
card.key_idea: An agent-based model using GPT-4o-mini agents with distinct biographies to track shifts in climate urgency and institutional trust via LLM-as-a-judge and LDA topic modeling.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using 10-agent populations with 10-20% committed minorities; measured via Euclidean jump distances and LDA. Results are compromised by LLM homogenization.
card.limitation: Strong LLM biases toward climate urgency and a tendency to avoid discussing institutional trust lead to homogenized, unrealistic discourse.

slides.title: Bayesian Belief Layer for Controllable Opinion Dynamics in LLM Agents
slides.tldr: CONTROLLABLE OPINION DYNAMICS IN LLM AGENTS
slides.highlight: Introduces Bayesian Chronicle Agents (BCA) to separate belief from speech, enabling controllable and auditable opinion dynamics in social simulations. This supports MIMIC's goals of simulating societal-scale impact analysis using LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: BCA introduces a Bayesian belief layer to make LLM agent opinion dynamics controllable and auditable.
card.key_idea: A separate belief layer uses a prior-strength parameter (κ) and Bayesian updates to decouple an agent's internal stance from its LLM-generated speech.
card.evaluation: Tested on four LLMs using synthetic policy questions; validated against classical DeGroot and Friedkin-Johnsen models with R² between 0.93 and 0.99.
card.limitation: Limited to one synthetic topic, binary stances, and a complete graph of 20 agents; not predictive of human trajectories.

slides.title: Identity Continuity in Long-Term Embodied AI Relationships: From Agent-Specific Identity Representation to Identity-Continuity Appraisal
slides.tldr: IDENTITY CONTINUITY IN LONG-TERM EMBODIED AI
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a framework for maintaining identity continuity in embodied AI through specific identity-content domains, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A framework for maintaining perceived identity continuity in long-term embodied AI despite system updates or migrations.
card.key_idea: Users evaluate identity via weighted evidence from three domains: embodied-perceptual, psychological-behavioral, and relational-autobiographical, influenced by shared history and relational roles.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: LLM-based Conversational AI Knowledge Assistant for MyBuddy Humanoid Robot
slides.tldr: LLM-POWERED CONVERSATIONAL ASSISTANT FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work implements an LLM-based assistant for a humanoid robot to enable natural, context-aware interaction and knowledge retrieval, supporting the RwB goal of advancing embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: An LLM-based conversational assistant for the MyBuddy humanoid robot enabling natural, knowledge-rich speech interactions.
card.key_idea: A cascading speech-to-speech architecture integrating Whisper-Fast (ASR), Llama 3.1 8B via Agno (reasoning), and Kokoro-82M (TTS) with external tool-calling for Wikipedia and arXiv.
card.evaluation: Qualitative dialogue experiments on diverse topics and quantitative measurement of LLM execution times (ranging from 12s to 42s).
card.limitation: Response times vary significantly based on query complexity and the need for external web searches.

slides.title: Capability-Aware Arbitration for Semantic Intent-Based Shared Control
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that balances human intent and robot capability to adapt authority, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on human-AI intent alignment and adaptive coaching.

card.one_liner: A shared-control framework that prevents over-helping by combining semantic intent and VLA execution capability confidence.
card.key_idea: Uses a VLM for semantic intent and a VLA for actions, blending authority via a sigmoid mapping of Bayesian-filtered intent confidence and trajectory-based capability confidence.
card.evaluation: 12 participants performed pick-and-place/stacking tasks (ID/OOD). Sem-Cap achieved 92% success, outperforming manual (83%) and intent-only (44%) baselines in success and friendliness.
card.limitation: Bayesian filtering creates a trade-off between temporal stability and responsiveness to genuine intent changes.

slides.title: Partner-Specific Affective Precision in Social Active Inference
slides.highlight: This work introduces affective precision as a relationship-specific metacognitive estimate of confidence, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and adapting to different human partners.

card.one_liner: Proposed framework distinguishes social prediction from policy commitment using relationship-specific confidence estimates called affective precision.
card.key_idea: Agents maintain per-partner generative models where predictive reliability (response surprisal) updates a local confidence signal, modulating policy precision to sharpen or flatten commitment to specific partners.
card.evaluation: Simulated via a multi-partner graded trust game; compared full precision against shared-precision and no-affect ablations using policy entropy and cumulative payoff.
card.limitation: Confidence is an auxiliary tracker, meaning accumulated confidence can lag behind abrupt social changes because the agent cannot infer when confidence is stale.

slides.title: SocioVerse2: A Longitudinal Dynamic Social Simulation Framework under a Human-AI Co-evolutionary Paradigm
slides.highlight: SocioVerse2 introduces a human-AI co-evolutionary paradigm for longitudinal social simulation, supporting counterfactual interventions and controllable research loops. This aligns with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: SocioVerse2 is a social simulation framework enabling longitudinal experiments through human-AI co-evolutionary research loops.
card.key_idea: It combines a longitudinal simulation loop for counterfactual branching via interventions with a controllable research loop for human-steered state editing and agentic infrastructure.
card.evaluation: Validated across three case families and seven studies, including reproducing ABMs, policy modeling, and macro-economic nowcasting using real-world grounding.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Mind or Message? Auditing Theory of Mind in Multi-Agent Social Simulation
slides.tldr: AUDITING THEORY OF MIND IN LLM AGENTS
slides.highlight: This research examines whether LLM agents in social simulations rely on actual models of a partner's mind or surface-level conversation records, which is relevant to MIMIC's use of agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: LLM agents exhibit surface social fluency but fail to maintain accurate internal models of partners' minds.
card.key_idea: A multi-issue negotiation audit using counterfactual probes on frozen transcripts to isolate egocentric projection from actual theory-of-mind inference.
card.evaluation: 160 dyads across 40 scenarios; measured Pareto optimality, joint value loss, and partner model accuracy via 2,880 probes. Results show high agreement but poor efficiency.
card.limitation: Uses synthetic, structurally regular scenarios and relies on verbal reports which may diverge from the agents' actual internal representations.

slides.title: MIRA: Real-Time Full-Duplex Human-Robot Interaction for Embodied Companions
slides.highlight: MIRA introduces a unified framework for real-time, interruptible human-robot interaction using a prefix-conditioned diffusion model for co-speech motion. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: MIRA enables real-time, full-duplex human-robot interaction with synchronized streaming co-speech motion and low-latency interruptions.
card.key_idea: A framework combining CORTEX (dual-timescale interaction policy), ROSCO (prefix-conditioned diffusion model for streaming audio-to-motion), and RHPC (inference scheme bounding physical commitment for responsiveness).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on BEAT dataset and Astribot S1 humanoid; demonstrated competitive audio-motion alignment and effective real-robot barge-in handling.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue
slides.tldr: SPEAKER-CENTERED DUAL-TRACK MEMORY FOR MULTI-PARTY DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: SpeakerMem-R1 addresses message attribution and relational understanding in multi-party settings using dual-track memory with person- and group-level views. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on identity recognition, diarization, and the perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: SpeakerMem-R1 uses dual-track memory to improve attribution and state reconstruction in multi-party dialogues.
card.key_idea: Combines a verbatim message track with a structured track (person- and group-level views), using a GRPO-trained Writer to manage memory updates and attribution.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on GroupMemBench, SocialMemBench, and EverMemBench using binary accuracy; outperformed mainstream frameworks by 3.3 to 12.4 percentage points.
card.limitation: Assumes reliable rosters and temporal identification; struggles with aliases, membership changes, implicit audiences, and parallel events.

slides.title: MSI-Bench: Evaluating Multi-Speaker Voice Interaction for Collaborative AI Agents
slides.highlight: This work introduces MSI-Bench to evaluate multi-speaker voice interaction, identifying critical needs for speaker-grounded perception and conversational restraint relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee modeling and social perception.

card.one_liner: MSI-Bench evaluates AI voice agents' ability to handle multi-speaker memory, instruction following, and reasoning.
card.key_idea: A bilingual benchmark of 1,152 scripted audio scenes testing speaker-grounded perception, authority constraints, selective disclosure, and conversational restraint using atomic rubrics and tool-call validation.
card.evaluation: 12 models evaluated via All-Pass Rate and Atomic Rubric Score; results show frontier models struggle with reasoning while open-weight models fail at perception.
card.limitation: Uses synthesized, scripted speech and lacks positive cases for selective engagement in bystander-speech metrics.

slides.title: Inferring the microscopic mechanisms of opinion dynamics using a kinetic Ising model
slides.tldr: EMPIRICAL VALIDATION OF KINETIC ISING MODELS FOR OPINION DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This research uses kinetic Ising models to infer transition probabilities in online social networks, providing a quantitative link between microscopic social behavior and macroscopic opinion dynamics. This is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and the modeling of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Empirical Twitter data validates that binary opinion dynamics are accurately described by kinetic Ising heat-bath dynamics.
card.key_idea: A hierarchy of four Ising models was tested; the best-performing model (M4) incorporates social influence, intrinsic bias, and degree-dependent temporal persistence.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using a year-long Twitter climate debate dataset via log-loss and Monte Carlo simulations. Results accurately reproduced response functions and macroscopic trajectories.
card.limitation: The study identifies correlations between network topology and persistence but does not establish the direction of causality.

slides.title: Toward Human-in-the-Loop Robot Failure Recovery: Bridging Communication Gaps in Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.highlight: This work introduces LD-HRI to evaluate how robots can bridge communication gaps when asking humans for help during failure recovery, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Introduces LD-HRI, a benchmark and dataset evaluating robot help requests across varying human listener knowledge levels.
card.key_idea: A web-based game where the same robot request is tested on 'Expert' (informed) and 'Novice' (uninformed) listeners across four tasks.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 446 human and 24 LLM requests via 1,302 listener trials; measured success, NASA-TLX workload, and inverse-semantics policies.
card.limitation: Does not establish a causal advantage for speaker types and cannot separate scene vs. part familiarity in the integrated task.

slides.title: CE$^4$L: Continual Ego, Exo, and Ego-Exo Learning
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for continual learning across ego and exo views, addressing cross-view correspondence and skill assessment relevant to the MOSAIC project's focus on ego-exo views and skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: CE4L is a multi-view continual learning benchmark for embodied agents with a competitive adapter-based baseline.
card.key_idea: VISTA uses lightweight task-specific adapters and a training-free router that assigns inputs based on residual distances to whitened subspaces derived from second-order statistics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four tasks (skill assessment, segmentation, association, planning) using EgoExoLearn; VISTA outperformed representative CL baselines across most metrics.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Designing Against Deskilling: Metacognitive Feedback Reduces Cognitive Offloading to LLM Assistants
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that metacognitive feedback can reduce cognitive offloading to LLMs and improve performance, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition in human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Metacognitive feedback reduces AI answer offloading and improves independent skill acquisition in fraction arithmetic.
card.key_idea: Comparing two interventions—metacognitive feedback (making offloading implications explicit) and effort-based rewards (incentivizing less assistance)—to prevent deskilling without restricting LLM access.
card.evaluation: Preregistered online experiment (N=704) using fraction arithmetic tasks and unaided tests; metacognitive feedback significantly improved performance, while rewards had no effect.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Voice-Light: A Full-Duplex Cascaded Voice Agent with Causal Turn-Taking and Speculative Generation
slides.tldr: FULL-DUPLEX VOICE AGENT WITH CAUSAL TURN-TAKING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a full-duplex voice agent focusing on causal turn-taking and speculative generation to handle overlaps and response timing. It is relevant to HyECHO's goals regarding addressee/listener modeling and the perception of hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: A full-duplex voice agent using a causal adapter and speculative generation to reduce response latency.
card.key_idea: Combines a shared-encoder causal turn-taking adapter with private speculative generation and a hybrid controller for reversible playback and audible-only conversation history.
card.evaluation: Tested on 1,673 real-conversation candidates and a 36-turn operator case study; learned turn-completion failed to beat Silero timing baselines.
card.limitation: Learned turn-taking transferred poorly from synthetic to human data; deployment study lacked diverse users, accents, and controlled environments.

slides.title: Towards Reliable Underwater Diver-Robot Interaction: Gesture Design, Interaction Logic, and Real-World Evaluation
slides.highlight: This research explores a closed-loop interaction framework using a seven-gesture vocabulary and command-level logic to improve robot recognition and usability. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A closed-loop underwater interaction framework balancing human gesture usability with machine-side recognition reliability.
card.key_idea: Integrates a seven-gesture vocabulary, lightweight landmark-based KNN recognition, and command-level logic (Hold-based authorization and temporal confirmation) to mitigate transient recognition errors.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via user study (30 participants) and robot experiments in a tank and pool; achieved 77.42% task-execution success rate.
card.limitation: Trade-offs exist between reducing false triggers and increasing missed commands or response latency.

slides.title: Adaptive Scaffolding Needs Contingency: An AI Tutor That Escalates and Fades on What the Learner Does
slides.highlight: The CoMeT system implements adaptive support that escalates and fades based on learner actions, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on agents that adapt at test time and monitor partner intent.

card.one_liner: CoMeT is an AI tutor that adjusts support levels based on learner performance to preserve metacognitive demand.
card.key_idea: The system uses a support ladder that escalates help when learners stall and fades (resets) when they demonstrate engagement or resolve a decision point.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects study with 131 adult learners on Python tasks. CoMeT matched the high demand of question-only tutors while reducing learner frustration.
card.limitation: Learners often did not answer directly, requiring the system to use model-based judgments to determine when to fade support.

slides.title: Chinese Startup Spirit AI Predicts Humanoid Robots Following Verbal Commands by Mid-2027
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOTS WITH VERBAL COMMAND CAPABILITIES
slides.highlight: Spirit AI predicts the arrival of humanoid robots capable of following verbal commands by mid-2027, relating to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Agility Robotics Unveils Digit 5 Humanoid Robot
slides.highlight: The introduction of the Digit 5 humanoid robot, designed to work with humans, is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Enriching Speech Emotion Representations with Conversational Context
slides.highlight: The ACERT module improves speech emotion recognition by integrating conversational context to capture emotional evolution. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement within human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: ACERT improves speech emotion recognition by integrating a flexible window of preceding conversational audio context.
card.key_idea: A module that uses temporal mean pooling to aggregate preceding audio context and fuses it with target utterance representations via a feed-forward network with residual connections.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on IEMOCAP, SAFE, and MELD using HuBERT-large. ACERT outperformed SOTA on IEMOCAP and established a context-aware benchmark on SAFE.
card.limitation: Ineffective on datasets with high emotional instability or rapid shifts, such as MELD, where context provides little benefit.

slides.title: Affective Shared Autonomy: Temporal Affect Dynamics and Subjective Evaluation in Bimanual Teleoperation Tasks
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework that modulates robotic assistance based on real-time operator affective states, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: An affect-aware shared autonomy framework for bimanual teleoperation that modulates robotic assistance based on real-time operator states.
card.key_idea: A multimodal fusion model combining facial video, cardiac signals, and arm kinematics to trigger assistance only during sustained adverse affective states (frustrated, stressed, fatigued, sad).
card.evaluation: User study (N=30) across three modes; measured state proportions and NASA-TLX. Proposed model outperformed zero-shot baselines (Qwen, MiniCPM-V) in state tracking.
card.limitation: Initial cognitive friction during adaptation and limited co-adaptation due to time-constrained laboratory protocols, slightly tempering overall user satisfaction.
